questions.stem: The average of 5 consecutive integers starting from 10 is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 7 — average of consecutive integers equals the middle term. Integers 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 → middle 12. Or sum 60 / 5 = 12.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Average age of 11 players is 22 years. On including the coach, the average rises to 23. The coach's age is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 2 — new member raises average by 1. Old sum = 11 × 22 = 242. New sum = 12 × 23 = 276. Coach = 276 − 242 = 34. Shortcut: new avg 23 + change contributed to old 11 members (11 × 1 = 11) = 34.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A class of 10 had an average of 75. A student scoring 50 left, and a new student joined, raising the average by 2. The new student's marks:
questions.explanation: TYPE 3 — replacement shifts average. Increase in sum = 10 × 2 = 20. New − old = 20 → new = 50 + 20 = 70.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The average of first 10 natural numbers is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 7 — formula for first n natural numbers: average = (n+1)/2 = 11/2 = 5.5. Sum = n(n+1)/2 = 55; 55/10 = 5.5.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A batsman's average after 20 innings is 30. He scores 50 in his 21st innings. His new average is:
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The average weight of A, B, C is 45 kg. If D joins them, the average becomes 40 kg. D weighs:
questions.explanation: TYPE 2 — new member drops average. Old sum = 135, new sum = 4 × 40 = 160. D = 160 − 135 = 25 kg. D is lighter than the average, so he pulls it down — sanity check matches.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Average of 8 numbers is 14. If each number is multiplied by 3, the new average is:
questions.explanation: Multiplying every term by k multiplies the average by k. 14 × 3 = 42. Similarly adding a constant to every term adds the same to the average.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The average of 11 numbers is 40. The average of the first 6 is 38 and of the last 6 is 44. The 6th number is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 8 — overlap trick. Sum of 11 = 440. Sum first 6 = 228. Sum last 6 = 264. 228 + 264 = 492 counts the 6th twice: 492 − 440 = 52.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
